Definition: of Hebrew origin (H1893); Abel, the son of Adam:--Abel.
BiblicalUsage: The New Testament remembers Abel as the first righteous man murdered and the first man commended for faith. Jesus says the blood ‘of righteous Abel’ will be required of His generation; Hebrews says ‘by faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain’; and his blood still speaks — set against the blood of Jesus, which ‘speaketh better things than that of Abel’.
TheologicalSignificance: Abel's blood cries for vengeance; Christ's blood speaks forgiveness — and Hebrews puts them side by side on purpose. I believe that is the whole gospel in one contrast: the first murder asks for justice, and the last sacrifice answers it, and the better blood is the one that speaks for me.
